result.title: UkrMeme: Multimodal Explainable Persuasion Detection in Ukrainian Memes
result.summary: Memes play a central role in modern online communication, especially in contexts of political conflict where visual and textual cues combine to convey persuasive messages. We study persuasive technique detection in Ukrainian memes using vision-language models (VLMs). We introduce UkrMeme, a dataset of 200 organically produced Ukrainian wartime memes annotated for persuasion techniques, and PTM-UA, a Ukrainian translation of a subset of the Propaganda 950 benchmark that preserves original visual content while translating meme text. We evaluate VLMs in a zero-shot prompting setup across image, text, and multimodal inputs using hierarchical F1 metrics. Finally, we compare Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) and model-generated token attributions and analyze the semantic categories of evidence emphasized by each explanation method.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建乌克兰战时梗图的说服技巧检测数据集 UkrMeme 与 Propaganda 950 的乌克兰语翻译子集 PTM-UA，在零样本提示下按图像、文本、多模态三种输入评测 VLM，并通过 LRP 与模型自生成 token 归因对比解释所强调证据的语义类别。
AI.relevance_reason: 其视觉与文本证据归因的对比方法可供核查：可能类比 LVR 中「答案是否真正使用视觉内容」与视觉旁路的诊断需求，但原文聚焦说服技巧检测与解释方法比较，未涉及 latent 推理状态。
